module purpose: neorv32_onewire is a bus-controlled serial engine that stores control settings, accepts transmit commands into a TX FIFO, generates timed 1-Wire waveforms on onewire_o, samples onewire_i into receive results, and reports status and completion through bus_rsp_o, clkgen_en_o, and irq_o.

use-case flows.value: control-register settings: enable, clear pulse, clock prescaler, and clock divider
transmit command word and payload written into the TX FIFO
clock ticks generated from the selected clock source and divider
serial command execution: fetch command, drive the wire, sample the wire, shift data, and detect presence
control and status fields returned on a control-register read
received byte and presence flag written into the RX FIFO and returned on a data-register read
interrupt asserted when the enabled controller has no pending TX entry and no serial transfer is busy
asynchronous reset clears control state, timing state, serial state, and output defaults

conceptual assets.concept: Controller enable setting for the 1-Wire block
conceptual assets.reasoning: A qualified control-register write stores ctrl.enable at line 142, reset forces it low at line 130, and the stored bit is then used to clear both FIFOs when disabled (lines 199 and 231), to gate interrupt generation (line 243), to stop or allow tick generation (lines 258-263), to feed the serial engine state bit (line 311), and to leave the entity on clkgen_en_o (line 273). The configure, operate, and report flows therefore depend on ctrl.enable retaining the written value. Availability is also established because the bit is held in ctrl.enable between writes and exported on clkgen_en_o.

A qualified control-register write stores ctrl.clear at line 143, line 140 clears it again on the next cycle, and the stored pulse is consumed in the FIFO-clear conditions at lines 199 and 231. The flush behavior of queued transmit and receive data therefore depends on the integrity of this request. Availability is established because the request is stored in ctrl.clear long enough to drive the clear conditions in the following clocked operation.

Qualified control-register writes store ctrl.clk_prsc and ctrl.clk_div at lines 144-145. The clock generator then selects clk_src indexed by ctrl.clk_prsc at line 260 and compares clk_cnt with unsigned(ctrl.clk_div) at line 261 to raise clk_tick at line 263 and clk_tick2 at line 268. The serial engine uses these ticks for command start, bit sampling, bit shifting, and reset/presence timing (lines 329, 346, 350, 360, 366, 374, 378). Integrity is established because wrong settings change the implemented 1-Wire timing; availability is established when ctrl.enable is set and the selected clk_src bit toggles.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmit command and payload queued for serial execution
conceptual assets.reasoning: A data-register write assembles fifo.tx_wdata from the command and payload bits at line 201 under the write qualifier of line 200. When the engine fetches a TX entry, fifo.tx_rdata is consumed to choose single-bit versus byte transfer length (lines 323-326), to load serial.sreg with the payload byte (line 328), and to select bit, byte, reset, or idle execution (lines 331-335). The operate flow and the waveform driven on the external wire therefore depend on the exact command and payload value. Availability is also established because fifo.tx_avail moves the engine out of idle at lines 317-318 and fifo.tx_re dequeues the entry at line 202.

conceptual assets.concept: Current serial transfer phase and busy/idle decision
conceptual assets.reasoning: serial.state is the held phase state of the engine: line 311 copies ctrl.enable into its high bit, lines 317-318 leave idle when a TX entry is available, lines 331-335 choose slot, reset, or idle from the fetched command, lines 354-356 end a data slot, lines 378-380 end a reset slot, and line 387 reinitializes the low bits in the fallback branch. serial.busy is then derived from serial.state at line 394. Integrity is established because TX dequeue (line 202), onewire_o control (lines 299-302), RX completion (lines 355 and 379), and irq generation (line 243) depend on this phase/busy state. Availability is established because the state is held in serial.state and updated on each qualified clocked transition.

conceptual assets.concept: Received 1-Wire result: sampled data byte and reset-presence flag
conceptual assets.reasoning: The engine captures onewire_i into serial.wire_in at line 296, samples a read slot into serial.sample at lines 346-347, shifts the sampled bit into serial.sreg at line 352, detects reset presence at lines 374-375, and packs serial.presence & serial.sreg into fifo.rx_wdata at line 232 for RX FIFO write on serial.done (line 233). The read-out flow therefore depends on the sampled byte and presence flag matching the captured wire value. Availability is established because serial.done causes the packed result to be written for later readback.

The engine drives onewire_o high when it is not busy or when serial.wire_hi is asserted (line 300), and drives it low when serial.wire_lo is asserted (line 302). serial.wire_lo is generated at command start and between data slots (lines 330 and 358); serial.wire_hi is generated at write-one or slot-end timing and at reset-end timing (lines 343 and 371). The external operate flow therefore depends on these stored drive decisions and the resulting onewire_o value. Availability is established because the decisions are regenerated on qualifying ticks while a transfer is active.

irq_o is computed each clock as ctrl.enable and not fifo.tx_avail and not serial.busy at line 243, with reset forcing 0 at line 241. The report flow depends on this event being asserted exactly when the enabled controller has no pending TX entry and no active serial transfer. Availability is established because the event is produced on the next clock whenever those RTL-visible conditions hold.
